title: Fushimi Inari on Foot
blurb: Walk Fushimi Inari under the real sun: from JR Inari station through the Romon, into the tunnels of the Senbon Torii, and up the mountain's path of torii to Yotsutsuji and the view of Kyoto.

weather.source: Kyoto: Japan Meteorological Agency, 1991-2020 normals, days with at least 0.5 mm

npcs.name: Kenta 健太
npcs.role: Shrine attendant, at the foot of the Omotesando
idle: Inari is the kami of rice, and so of business. That's why companies give torii: for a good year.
There are about thirty thousand Inari shrines in Japan. This is the head one.

npcs.name: Mrs. Ota 太田
idle: Inari-zushi: rice in fried tofu. The foxes love fried tofu, they say, so we do too.
Keep right in the torii. Up on the right, down on the left.

npcs.name: Daichi 大地
idle: Most people turn back here. The view is the reward: all of Kyoto to the west.
Up to the summit and round is another hour. More torii, more foxes, more steps.

quests.title: The gate of the foxes
talk: ようお参り, welcome to Fushimi Inari. Straight up the Omotesando is the Romon, given by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1589.
The foxes either side of it are Inari's messengers: a jewel, and the key to the rice store. Go through the gate and past the halls to the Senbon Torii; Mrs. Ota's shop is at the entrance.

steps.text: Walk up the Omotesando to the Romon and its foxes
Find Mrs. Ota at the entrance of the Senbon Torii

quests.title: A thousand gates
talk: The Senbon Torii: two tunnels, up on the right, down on the left. Someone counted 382 in one and 399 in the other.
Go on up past the Okusha. Daichi is resting at Yotsutsuji, halfway up; he'll show you the view.

steps.text: Climb the mountain path to Daichi at Yotsutsuji

quests.title: Kyoto from the mountain
talk: You made it. Look west: the whole city, and Kyoto Tower if you look hard.
From here the path goes round the summit, 233 m. Or back down through the torii: you'll see the names written on their backs.

steps.text: Look out over Kyoto from Yotsutsuji

spots.name: The Romon and its foxes 楼門
lines: Toyotomi Hideyoshi gave this gate in 1589, they say in thanks for his mother's recovery.
The foxes are Inari's messengers. One holds a jewel; the other the key to the rice store.

spots.name: Senbon Torii 千本鳥居
lines: Two tunnels side by side: you keep to the right one going up. Each torii was given by a person or a company; their names are on the back.
Look back down the way you came: from above, the black writing on every torii shows.

spots.name: Yotsutsuji 四ツ辻
lines: Halfway up, the mountain opens to the west: all of Kyoto, and on a clear evening the sun going down over Arashiyama.
From here the path goes round the summit. 一ノ峰, the top, is 233 m.
About ten thousand on the whole mountain.
And all the way to the top?
Two, three hours there and back. Yotsutsuji has the view, if your legs give up.
